description: The global Sentinel-2 land-cover raster at 10 m, drawn by the very ImageServer that measures the figures: one source read twice.

options.content:
# Land use and land cover — Sentinel-2 10 m

The figures come from `computeHistograms`, which counts pixels per class over **the extent the map is showing**: pan or zoom, anywhere in the world, and everything below is recomputed in half a second.

**And the map now comes from that same service.** The background is the ImageServer drawing the land cover on demand, not a copy: map and numbers read one source, so they cannot drift apart.

**The two years of the comparison, on the map.** *Year A* and *Year B* choose which two years everything is measured between: the map carries one layer of each — A below, B on top — and the relative change down here is computed between exactly those two, not between the first and last of the series. Since B covers A, split the viewer with the first button in the map's control column to compare them: **Swipe** gives a vertical bar you drag from one year to the other. The composition by year, further down, still shows all nine.

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | [Sentinel-2 10m Land Use/Land Cover Time Series](https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=cfcb7609de5f478eb7666240902d4d3d) · **Impact Observatory, Microsoft and Esri**. Licensed CC BY 4.0, anonymous access |
| Coverage | Worldwide, 10 m, nine classes, 2017-2025 |
| How it arrives | Figures: `computeHistograms` → Infinity. Background: `exportImage`, one request per tile, with the service's own palette |

**One service, not two hundred files.** An ImageServer is a *mosaic dataset*: the catalogue of its rasters, the rule for choosing between them, and a pyramid built over the whole set. That is why it answers for any extent at any zoom from a single endpoint — the entire planet in one layer, in little over a second per tile. The same collection split into COGs is some two hundred files per year, one per UTM zone.

**The years come from the source.** The selector carries no hand-written list: it asks the service's catalogue which years it publishes. They are the same nine the figures are measured over, with no drift.

**What you need to know so as not to misread the figures:**

- **Impact Observatory advises against pixel-by-pixel comparison between years.** Each year is classified separately and the model changes; part of the year-on-year difference is method, not territory. That is why this board leads with **relative change**, which holds up best.
- **The sampling runs on a Web Mercator grid, so area is biased by latitude.** Each sample covers `(scale·cos φ)²` of real ground: at 60° of latitude, a quarter of what it covers at the equator. The km² are **approximate**, and the more so — optimistically — for high-latitude classes the higher the view reaches. **Relative change does not carry that bias**, because all nine years are measured on the same grid.
- **The "Clouds" class is the year's quality thermometer.** When it rises, the rest of that year's classes are worth less. In testing it swings between 0.2 % and 1.8 % depending on the year and the region.

**Narrowing by drawing.** The map's draw tool (polygon or rectangle) replaces the view's extent with the shape: the figures come to describe only what the shape encloses, at the finest resolution the service allows. Delete the shape to go back to the view.

*The service cuts off at 4000 px a side and at ~13 M cells. Above 4000 it returns `{"histograms":[]}` **with no error**; above 13 M it returns an explicit 400. The hidden `escala` variable keeps the request at 3500 px a side, so neither ceiling should be reached.*


**A single class, with one click.** The **Land cover class** dropdown — or a click on the class in the relative-change gauge or in the detail table — leaves **both layers** showing that cover alone: the chosen class is common to both years, which is what lets you look at how it changed. The panel does not draw it: the service publishes a render function per class, and what arrives is the class in its colour with the rest of the raster **transparent**, so what shows underneath is the base map, not a hole. The figures do not move: they go on measuring **all** the classes, so that isolating is for looking and is not confused with filtering. Go back to *All* to recover the whole map.

panels.description: The background is the 10 m raster of Azuay, tiled by titiler over the GeoTIFFs in `testdata/lulc/`; the "Raster year" selector changes it. Above it, switched off, nine `bitmap` layers with the whole planet at ~10 km per pixel: turn one on to leave Azuay, turn them off to come back to the detail.

-- Un servicio, no doscientos ficheros.
--
-- El ImageServer es un mosaic dataset: el catálogo de sus rásteres, la regla
-- para elegir entre ellos y una pirámide sobre el conjunto. Responde para
-- cualquier extensión y cualquier zoom desde un solo punto final, así que
-- desaparecen el bloque de zonas UTM, la firma SAS y el servidor de teselas.
--
-- Y es el MISMO servicio del que salen las cifras de abajo, de modo que mapa y
-- números no pueden desacompasarse: son una fuente leída dos veces.
SELECT
  'https://ic.imagery1.arcgis.com/arcgis/rest/services/Sentinel2_10m_LandCover/ImageServer' AS esri_url,
  '{"mosaicMethod":"esriMosaicAttribute","where":"Year=' || CAST($anioA AS VARCHAR) || '"}' AS mosaic_rule,

  -- Y así es como se aísla una clase: el propio servicio publica una función
  -- «Isolate …» por cobertura, que devuelve esa clase con su color y TODO lo
  -- demás transparente. No se filtra nada aquí ni se recorta el ráster; se le
  -- pide otro dibujo. Vacío quiere decir «la cartográfica», que es la de siempre.
  --
  -- `$clase` va sin comillas: este datasource ya entrecomilla las variables, y
  -- '$clase' saldría como ''pct_arboles'' y sería un error de sintaxis. Se acepta
  -- Se le quita el prefijo porque cada panel nombra sus campos a su manera
  -- (`pct_` en el gráfico, `km2_` en la tabla), y se acepta además la etiqueta en
  -- español, que es lo que manda el clic en el medidor de cambio relativo.
  CASE
    WHEN regexp_replace($clase, '^(pct_|km2_)', '') IN ('arboles', 'Árboles')
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Trees for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN regexp_replace($clase, '^(pct_|km2_)', '') IN ('pastizal', 'Pastizal/Matorral')
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Rangelands Areas for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN regexp_replace($clase, '^(pct_|km2_)', '') IN ('cultivos', 'Cultivos')
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Crops for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN regexp_replace($clase, '^(pct_|km2_)', '') IN ('construido', 'Área construida')
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Built Areas for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN regexp_replace($clase, '^(pct_|km2_)', '') IN ('suelo_desnudo', 'Suelo desnudo')
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Bare Ground Areas for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN regexp_replace($clase, '^(pct_|km2_)', '') IN ('agua', 'Agua')
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Water Areas for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN regexp_replace($clase, '^(pct_|km2_)', '') IN ('veg_inundada', 'Vegetación inundada')
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Flooded Vegeation Areas for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN regexp_replace($clase, '^(pct_|km2_)', '') IN ('nieve', 'Nieve/Hielo')
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Snow or Ice for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN regexp_replace($clase, '^(pct_|km2_)', '') IN ('nubes', 'Nubes')
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Clouds for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN $clase IN ('convertidas', 'Tierras convertidas')
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Converted Lands for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    ELSE ''
  END AS rendering_rule

list.definition: Años que publica el catálogo del ImageServer
list.description: El año de partida de la comparación. Sale del catálogo del propio servicio.
list.label: Year A (below)
list.name: anioA
list.query:
-- Los años los publica el propio servicio: su catálogo es una tabla y lleva
-- un campo `Year`. Nueve hoy, los mismos que miden las cifras.
WITH resp AS (
  SELECT http_get(
    'https://ic.imagery1.arcgis.com/arcgis/rest/services/Sentinel2_10m_LandCover/ImageServer/query'
    || '?where=1%3D1&outFields=Year&returnDistinctValues=true'
    || '&returnGeometry=false&orderByFields=Year&f=json'
  ) AS r
),
filas AS (SELECT unnest(json_extract(r->>'body', '$.features[*]')) AS f FROM resp)
SELECT DISTINCT CAST(f->'attributes'->>'Year' AS VARCHAR) AS anio
FROM filas
WHERE f->'attributes'->>'Year' IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY anio DESC

list.label: Sampling scale (m)
list.name: escala
list.query:
WITH v AS (
  SELECT length('$area') > 8 AS dibujado,
         try_cast('$mapWest' AS DOUBLE) AS w, try_cast('$mapEast' AS DOUBLE) AS e,
         try_cast('$mapSouth' AS DOUBLE) AS s, try_cast('$mapNorth' AS DOUBLE) AS n
), c AS (
  SELECT dibujado,
         CASE WHEN dibujado THEN ST_XMin(ST_GeomFromText('$area'))
              WHEN coalesce(e,180.0) <= coalesce(w,-180.0) THEN -180.0 ELSE coalesce(w,-180.0) END AS w0,
         CASE WHEN dibujado THEN ST_XMax(ST_GeomFromText('$area'))
              WHEN coalesce(e,180.0) <= coalesce(w,-180.0) THEN  180.0 ELSE coalesce(e, 180.0) END AS e0,
         CASE WHEN dibujado THEN greatest(-80.0134, ST_YMin(ST_GeomFromText('$area')))
              ELSE greatest(-80.0134, least(84.0326, coalesce(s,-80.0134))) END AS s0,
         CASE WHEN dibujado THEN least(84.0326, ST_YMax(ST_GeomFromText('$area')))
              ELSE greatest(-80.0134, least(84.0326, coalesce(n, 84.0326))) END AS n0
  FROM v
), d AS (
  SELECT dibujado, w0, e0, s0, n0,
         CASE WHEN e0 <= w0 THEN 360.0 ELSE least(360.0, e0 - w0) END AS dlon,
         (ln(tan((90 + greatest(n0, s0 + 0.0005)) * pi()/360))
          - ln(tan((90 + s0) * pi()/360))) / (pi()/180) AS dmerc
  FROM c
), e AS (
  SELECT *, greatest(dlon * 111319.490793 / 3500, dmerc * 111319.490793 / 3500, 10.0) AS escala FROM d
)
SELECT printf('%.4f', escala) AS escala FROM e

list.label: Area per sample (km²)
list.name: areaPx
list.query:
WITH v AS (
  SELECT length('$area') > 8 AS dibujado,
         try_cast('$mapWest' AS DOUBLE) AS w, try_cast('$mapEast' AS DOUBLE) AS e,
         try_cast('$mapSouth' AS DOUBLE) AS s, try_cast('$mapNorth' AS DOUBLE) AS n
), c AS (
  SELECT dibujado,
         CASE WHEN dibujado THEN ST_XMin(ST_GeomFromText('$area'))
              WHEN coalesce(e,180.0) <= coalesce(w,-180.0) THEN -180.0 ELSE coalesce(w,-180.0) END AS w0,
         CASE WHEN dibujado THEN ST_XMax(ST_GeomFromText('$area'))
              WHEN coalesce(e,180.0) <= coalesce(w,-180.0) THEN  180.0 ELSE coalesce(e, 180.0) END AS e0,
         CASE WHEN dibujado THEN greatest(-80.0134, ST_YMin(ST_GeomFromText('$area')))
              ELSE greatest(-80.0134, least(84.0326, coalesce(s,-80.0134))) END AS s0,
         CASE WHEN dibujado THEN least(84.0326, ST_YMax(ST_GeomFromText('$area')))
              ELSE greatest(-80.0134, least(84.0326, coalesce(n, 84.0326))) END AS n0
  FROM v
), d AS (
  SELECT dibujado, w0, e0, s0, n0,
         CASE WHEN e0 <= w0 THEN 360.0 ELSE least(360.0, e0 - w0) END AS dlon,
         (ln(tan((90 + greatest(n0, s0 + 0.0005)) * pi()/360))
          - ln(tan((90 + s0) * pi()/360))) / (pi()/180) AS dmerc
  FROM c
), e AS (
  SELECT *, greatest(dlon * 111319.490793 / 3500, dmerc * 111319.490793 / 3500, 10.0) AS escala FROM d
)
SELECT printf('%.12f', 6371007.0 * escala * escala
                       * (sin(radians(n0)) - sin(radians(s0)))
                       / (dmerc * 111319.490793) / 1e6) AS area_px FROM e

list.label: Geometry (Esri JSON)
list.name: geom
list.query:
WITH v AS (
  SELECT length('$area') > 8 AS dibujado,
         try_cast('$mapWest' AS DOUBLE) AS w, try_cast('$mapEast' AS DOUBLE) AS e,
         try_cast('$mapSouth' AS DOUBLE) AS s, try_cast('$mapNorth' AS DOUBLE) AS n
), c AS (
  SELECT dibujado,
         CASE WHEN dibujado THEN ST_XMin(ST_GeomFromText('$area'))
              WHEN coalesce(e,180.0) <= coalesce(w,-180.0) THEN -180.0 ELSE coalesce(w,-180.0) END AS w0,
         CASE WHEN dibujado THEN ST_XMax(ST_GeomFromText('$area'))
              WHEN coalesce(e,180.0) <= coalesce(w,-180.0) THEN  180.0 ELSE coalesce(e, 180.0) END AS e0,
         CASE WHEN dibujado THEN greatest(-80.0134, ST_YMin(ST_GeomFromText('$area')))
              ELSE greatest(-80.0134, least(84.0326, coalesce(s,-80.0134))) END AS s0,
         CASE WHEN dibujado THEN least(84.0326, ST_YMax(ST_GeomFromText('$area')))
              ELSE greatest(-80.0134, least(84.0326, coalesce(n, 84.0326))) END AS n0
  FROM v
), d AS (
  SELECT dibujado, w0, e0, s0, n0,
         CASE WHEN e0 <= w0 THEN 360.0 ELSE least(360.0, e0 - w0) END AS dlon,
         (ln(tan((90 + greatest(n0, s0 + 0.0005)) * pi()/360))
          - ln(tan((90 + s0) * pi()/360))) / (pi()/180) AS dmerc
  FROM c
), e AS (
  SELECT *, greatest(dlon * 111319.490793 / 3500, dmerc * 111319.490793 / 3500, 10.0) AS escala FROM d
)
SELECT CASE WHEN dibujado
       THEN '{"rings":' || json_extract(ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_GeomFromText('$area')), '$.coordinates')::VARCHAR
            || ',"spatialReference":{"wkid":4326}}'
       ELSE '{"xmin":' || w0 || ',"ymin":' || s0 || ',"xmax":' || e0 || ',"ymax":' || n0
            || ',"spatialReference":{"wkid":4326}}'
       END AS geom FROM e
